title: One Hacked IT Tool, Many Hacked Companies: The N-central Flaw (CVE-2026-86218)
description:
How can one hacked IT tool reach hundreds of companies? Many IT providers manage their customers' computers from one remote monitoring and management (RMM) console. If that console is compromised, every connected computer is in reach.

Real example: N-able N-central. On September 5, 2026, N-able released N-central 2026.3 Hotfix 4 (build 2026.3.1.14) to fix CVE-2026-86218, a critical flaw that allows pre-authentication remote code execution on the N-central server.

Timeline
- September 4: Huntress investigated a compromise of a customer's N-central server. Because of limited logging, it cannot confirm which flaw was used.
- September 5: N-able shipped Hotfix 4.
- September 8: the US agency CISA added CVE-2026-86218 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, with a September 11 deadline for US federal agencies. N-able told customers the flaw has been observed being exploited in the wild.

Between August 2 and September 5, N-able patched five N-central security flaws across four hotfixes.

If your company self-hosts N-central: update to 2026.3 Hotfix 4 or later. N-able says hosted customers were already patched.

Four questions for your IT provider:
1. Is your management tool patched, and how fast?
2. Is its login hidden from the open internet?
3. Would you notice a new admin account?
4. Do you review its logs and remote sessions?
